Google Cloud Icons — usage rules (brand guidelines, reference use)

Source: Official Google Cloud Icon Library (https://cloud.google.com/icons)

Google permits the product icons to be used freely and without permission to
accurately reference Google's technology and tools (for instance in books or
architecture diagrams). Use is governed by Google's brand/trademark guidelines:
  - Permitted: reference Google Cloud products in architecture diagrams, docs,
    and training materials.
  - Uniform scaling only (width = height). Do NOT distort, recolor, or crop the
    icons — the brand guidelines forbid distortion (proportional scaling is OK).
  - Do not imply Google affiliation, sponsorship, or endorsement.
  - Do not represent a Google Cloud service as your own product or service.

This project is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Google LLC.
Google Cloud and the Google Cloud logo are trademarks of Google LLC.

Coverage (read me)
------------------
The "core products" icon pack is narrow on purpose — it ships about 19 product
glyphs. Common services NOT in the pack include:
  - Cloud Load Balancing
  - Cloud CDN
  - Pub/Sub
  - Memorystore
(Plus less-frequent gaps: Cloud Build, Cloud Tasks, Workflows, Cloud
Functions, plus most networking + observability glyphs. Always check
INDEX.md first — if a service appears missing, confirm it isn't shipped
before applying the fallback ladder.)

When a needed service is missing, prefer (in order):
  1. A labeled rectangle without an icon.
  2. A nearest-meaning Google Cloud icon with an explicit label override.
  3. A FluentUI generic icon (Globe / Database / Queue).

Tag the fallback in the diagram with a single header comment so reviewers know
the gap is intentional, e.g. "' coverage-note: GCP missing icon for X".
